_comment: C0-12 pipedream bodies EN, updated 2026-11-21 with Workflows shutdown and Connect docs. 正文「相关条目」1 行带 .md 链接（zapier），related 写 1 条。

axes.model_access: Workflow steps can connect to each vendor's LLMs (official AI-integration docs line); Connect lets an app or AI agent call any AI API / LLM. The signature trait is code-first automation: steps can be written in Node/Python/Bash. Pipedream is not a model provider.
axes.runtime: Pipedream hosts a serverless runtime and workflow service; Connect's API, SDK, MCP Servers and API Proxy also run on the platform. The local CLI is for development and deployment; the official material does not claim a full self-hosted form.
axes.local_files: Execution happens on Pipedream's cloud; locally you develop via CLI/SDK. Connect credentials and tokens are sent over HTTPS and encrypted at rest on the platform. Workflow structures can be exported as JSON with the official export tool; the platform does not run local models.
axes.background: The hosted serverless runtime carries schedules, webhooks, event queues and retries while your machine is off. Workflows has been in maintenance mode since 2026 and shuts down on 2027-03-31; Connect is not affected.
axes.tools: Connect provides a client SDK, managed auth for 2,500+ APIs, 10k prebuilt tools/triggers, MCP Servers and an API Proxy; the workflow side has code steps and a source-available component registry.
axes.context: The platform keeps no conversation memory: Connect identifies an end user via external_user_id and fetches that user's token per call. Cross-call conversation history and app state are the caller's responsibility; the platform persistence surface is the connected account and workflow configuration.
axes.permissions: Connect accepts OAuth/API keys via Pipedream's approved OAuth clients or your own; credentials are sent over HTTPS and encrypted at rest, and Pipedream can provide a SOC 2 Type 2 report and HIPAA BAA. Workflows credentials and OAuth tokens will be permanently deleted by 2027-04-30.
axes.fit: Fits: developers adding third-party integrations to apps or AI agents (Connect line); automation teams wanting code-level control with a hosted runtime. Does not fit: teams that never touch code; those requiring full self-hosting; or users treating Workflows as a long-term production platform without planning the 2027 migration.

runs: No measured workflow-building runs. The entry covers platform capability, auth boundaries and the official shutdown timeline. Connect's 2,500+ APIs, 10k tools/triggers, MCP, API Proxy and credential-encryption statements come from the official Connect Overview; the Workflows shutdown and data deletion come from the official Workflows document.
unknowns:
- The full per-repo source-available licence picture (not verified repo by repo)
- Coverage limits of the Workflows export tool for complex workflows and history (check the official export docs)
- Self-hosted form (no official statement)
- Recoverability of Workflows data other than through Connect after 2027-03-31 (the official notice says permanent deletion)
related: Form-style vs code-style contrast: both connector automation — Pipedream treats code as a first-class citizen.
